title: Wally now serves ten open models
summary: The Wally catalog now lists ten open models, including Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3 and the DeepSeek V4 family. Fast versions have their own model ids, and Eve answers questions with a probability for each answer.
body_markdown:
Wally by RunAnywhere gives you one CLI and one API key for frontier open models. Today we are publishing the Wally catalog: ten models, all behind the same key, the same CLI and the same OpenAI-compatible API.


## What changed


- **Ten models in one catalog.** Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3 and the DeepSeek V4 family are all live.
- **Fast mode has its own ids.** You pick speed by picking a model id.
- **Eve, a decision model.** It scores questions and returns a probability for each answer.
- **A live catalog endpoint.** The current list is always at[inference.runanywhere.ai/v1/models/catalog](https://inference.runanywhere.ai/v1/models/catalog) .

## What fast mode means


Fast mode is the same model, served for speed. Use it for agent loops, voice, and anything a person sits and waits on.


Each fast model has its own id. To switch, change the` model` field in your request or the` -m` flag in the CLI. Nothing else in your code changes.


The[pricing page](https://runwally.com/pricing) has the current rates for every model id.


## Eve


Eve is a decision model. You ask it a yes/no, multiple-choice or scored question, and it returns a probability for each answer. That makes it useful when your code needs a judgment it can branch on.


Run it from the CLI with` wally decisions` . The[Wally docs](https://docs.runanywhere.ai/) cover the options.


## Use it from a coding agent


The CLI connects coding agents like OpenCode, Claude Code and Codex to any model in the catalog. Sign in once, then start an agent on a hosted model:


bash


```text
1  wally account login    2  wally opencode --cloud -m glm-5.3-fast
```


Hosted commands always carry` --cloud` . Swap the` -m` value for any id in the table above.


## Use it from your own code


The API is OpenAI-compatible. Point the OpenAI SDK at Wally's base URL and pick a model id:


python


```text
1  import   os    2   from   openai   import   OpenAI    3
4  client   =   OpenAI  (  base_url  =  "https://inference.runanywhere.ai/v1"  ,   api_key  =  os  .  environ  [  "WALLY_API_KEY"  ]  )     5  reply   =   client  .  chat  .  completions  .  create  (  model  =  "glm-5.3-flash"  ,   messages  =  [  {  "role"  :     "user"  ,     "content"  :     "Explain a hash map in two sentences."  }  ]  )     6   print  (  reply  .  choices  [  0  ]  .  message  .  content  )
```


Calling the API directly needs an API key from your account. The[Wally docs](https://docs.runanywhere.ai/) explain how to create one.


## Your data


Production Wally does not store prompt or completion bodies.


## Get started


1. Sign in to the[console](https://console.runanywhere.ai/) and buy prepaid credits. Usage is paid from those credits.
2. Check the rates on the[pricing page](https://runwally.com/pricing) .
3. Follow the[setup guide in the docs](https://docs.runanywhere.ai/) , or run` wally account login` and start an agent.


More about Wally is at[runwally.com](https://runwally.com/) .
